extracted.intended_audience: national IP offices, patent attorneys/agents, applicants, and government policymakers in OAPI Member States
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing filing, examination, registration, publication, enforcement, institutional powers, and procedural requirements for patents, utility models, trademarks, designs, plant varieties and other IP in the African Intellectual Property Organization (Bangui Agreement). Applies to applicants, agents, national ministries and OAPI organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and responsibilities of the Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The African Intellectual Property Organization shall be responsible for implementing and applying the common administrative procedures deriving from a uniform system for the protection of industrial property and the provisions of relevant international agreements to which the Member States have acceded, and providing services related to industrial property; contributing to the promotion of protection for literary and artistic property; stimulating creation of collective management organizations; centralizing, coordinating and disseminating information relating to protection of literary and artistic property; promoting economic development through effective protection of IP and related rights; providing training on IP; performing other duties connected with its aims; promoting technological innovation and creativity; promoting protection of geographical indications, traditional cultural expressions and traditional knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 2 enumerates (a)–(k) as discrete responsibilities; these functions guide OAPI's service, outreach, training, and policy roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI serves as national industrial property office
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Member State, the Organization shall serve both as the national industrial property service and as the central office for patent documentation and information, within the meaning of Article 12 of the Paris Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 3(1) — OAPI acts in place of national IP offices for Member States unless otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI as PCT national/receiving/designated/elected office
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Member State party to the Patent Cooperation Treaty, the Organization shall serve as 'national office', 'designated office', 'elected office' or 'receiving office' within the meaning of the relevant articles of that Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 3(2) — OAPI functions for international (PCT) procedures for its Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI as office of origin and designated office under Madrid Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Member State, the Organization shall serve as 'office of origin' and 'designated office' within the meaning of the relevant articles of the Protocol Relating to the Madrid Agreement Concerning the International Registration of Marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 3(3) — OAPI handles Madrid Protocol-related national functions for Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution jurisdiction — national courts primary
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided in an agreement, disputes relating to recognition, scope or exploitation of the rights provided for in this Agreement and its annexes shall fall within the jurisdiction of courts in Member States; these courts shall have exclusive jurisdiction over related criminal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 4(1) — default forum is domestic courts of Member States; criminal matters exclusively for those courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration and mediation option for disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute concerning the application of this Agreement and its annexes may be settled by arbitration or mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 4(2) — parties may resort to alternative dispute resolution when not precluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights are independent national rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights relating to the fields of intellectual property, as provided for in the annexes to this Agreement, shall be independent national rights subject to the legislation of each Member State in which they have effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5(1) — although administered regionally, rights remain national in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement and annexes serve as law in Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement and its annexes shall serve as laws governing their intended subject matter in the Member States, where they shall rescind or prevent the entry into force of all contrary provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5(2) — Bangui Agreement and annexes supersede conflicting national provisions; Annex VII (literary and artistic property) is a minimum statutory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment for non-nationals subject to reciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-nationals shall enjoy the provisions of this Agreement and its annexes under the same conditions as nationals, applying also to non-nationals of a State party to an international agreement to which the Organization or its Member States are parties or non-nationals who do not have their principal establishment or residence in such a State under conditions of reciprocity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5(3)–(4) — treatment of foreigners depends on reciprocity and treaty status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex structure and subject-matter coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The annexes to this Agreement contain the provisions to be applied in each Member State concerning patents (Annex I), utility models (Annex II), trademarks and service marks (Annex III), industrial designs (Annex IV), trade names (Annex V), geographical indications (Annex VI), literary and artistic property (Annex VII), protection against unfair competition (Annex VIII), layout designs (topographies) of integrated circuits (Annex IX), and plant variety protection (Annex X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 6(1) — Annexes I–X form integral part and specify sectoral rules and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to implement international treaties' administrative procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: By decision of the Administrative Council, the Organization may take any measures for the application of the administrative procedures necessary for the implementation of the international treaties concerning intellectual property to which the Member States have acceded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 7 — Administrative Council empowers OAPI to operationalize treaty obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing location — direct filing with the Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for patents, utility models, trademarks or service marks, industrial designs, trade names, geographical indications or layout designs and applications for plant variety certificates shall be filed directly with the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8(1) — default filing is direct with OAPI; implementing regs may detail formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate filing via competent Ministry and transmission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be filed with the competent Ministry of a Member State where the applicant is domiciled; in such case the Ministry shall transmit the application to the Organization within five working days of receiving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8(2) — Ministries act as depositories and must forward filings promptly (5 working days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal filing receipt/report to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A report, of which a copy shall be provided to the applicant, shall be prepared by the Organization or by the Ministry, taking formal note of each filing and stating the date and time of the submission of the documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8(3) — applicants receive documentary proof of filing date/time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory local agent for applicants resident outside Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants resident outside the territory of the Member States shall file through an agent selected in one of those Member States; professional status of agents accredited to the Organization governed by special regulations adopted by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8(4) — foreign applicants require an in-territory agent; agent accreditation regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted means of transmission of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed with the Organization or the Ministry may be conveyed by postal, electronic or any other legal means of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8(5) — multiple communication channels accepted, including electronic.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI as PCT receiving office and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall act as receiving office within the meaning of the Patent Cooperation Treaty with respect to international applications filed by residents and nationals of Member States, save where an agreement has been concluded that another office shall act instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 8(6)(a)–(b) — OAPI is PCT receiving office unless contracted otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of filing — regional national filing effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any filing with the Ministry of one of the Member States in accordance with this Agreement and its annexes, or with the Organization, shall be equivalent to a national filing in each Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 9(1) — a single filing has effect across Member States as a national filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications and registrations produce national effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Any filing of an international patent application that includes the designation of at least one Member State shall be equivalent to a national filing in each Member State party to the Patent Cooperation Treaty; similarly, international registrations under Madrid or Hague that include designation of at least one Member State shall have effect as national deposits in Member States party to those treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 9(2)–(4) — interplay with PCT, Madrid, Hague produces national effects when Member States are also party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination, grant and publication procedures for patents and utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine applications for patents and utility models according to the common procedure provided for in this Agreement and its Annexes I and II; it shall grant patents and register utility models and ensure their publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10(1)–(2) — OAPI conducts substantive/regulatory examination and publishes results per annex procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT procedural interplay for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure before the Organization with regard to international applications filed in accordance with the rules of the Patent Cooperation Treaty shall be subject to the provisions of that Treaty, complemented by those of this Agreement and its Annex I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10(3) — PCT rules govern, supplemented by Bangui/Annex I where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of patents and utility models in Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: In each Member State, utility models and, subject to provisions, patents shall produce the effects provided for in this Agreement and its Annex II; patents granted from international applications shall produce effects in Member States that are also party to the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10(4)–(5) — territorial effect depends on membership and treaty participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation agreements with partner offices
rubrics_metrics.description: By unanimous decision of the Administrative Council, the Organization may enter into validation agreements with partner offices, in particular on the recognition of deposits, results of examinations and titles granted; conditions fixed by implementing regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 10(6) — OAPI can recognize external examination results/titles by agreement (validation mechanism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination, registration and effects for trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine, register and publish trademarks and service marks according to the common procedure provided for in this Agreement and its Annex III; registered and published marks shall produce their effects in each Member State in accordance with this Agreement and Annex III; international registrations under Madrid producing effect in at least one Member State have same effects as if registered with the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 11 — registration and territorial effects rules for marks; Madrid interplay noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination, registration and effects for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine, register, maintain and publish industrial designs according to the common procedure in this Agreement and Annex IV; registered and published designs produce effects in each Member State; international deposit under the Hague Agreement producing effect in at least one Member State shall have same effects as deposit with the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 12 — Hague Agreement interplay and Annex IV procedures govern designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and effects for trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine, register, maintain and publish trade names according to the common procedure provided for in this Agreement and its Annex V; registered and published trade names shall produce their effects in each Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 13 — trade name registration and territorial effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and effects for geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine, register and publish geographical indications according to the common procedure provided for in this Agreement and its Annex VI; registered and published geographical indications shall produce their effects in each Member State; international registration under the Lisbon Agreement having effect in at least one Member State shall produce same effects as if registered with the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 14 — geographical indications governed by Annex VI and Lisbon Agreement interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and effects for layout designs (topographies) of integrated circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine, register, maintain and publish layout designs of integrated circuits according to the common procedure provided for in this Agreement and its Annex IX; registered and published layout designs shall produce their effects in each Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 15 — Annex IX governs topographies registration and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination, issuance and effects for plant variety certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine applications for plant variety certificates, issue, maintain and publish such certificates according to the common procedure provided for in this Agreement and its Annex X; registered and published new plant varieties shall produce their effects in each Member State in accordance with Annex X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 16 — Annex X sets substantive and procedural rules for plant variety protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and Official Bulletin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish under conditions set forth in implementing regulations: (a) titles of any kind; (b) all titles issued; (c) any subsequent procedural documents; and (d) any document amending or assigning the rights in the titles. Titles issued shall be published in the Official Bulletin of Industrial Property; all publications transmitted to the Ministry of each Member State responsible for industrial property, literary and artistic property or plant varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 17 — publication obligations and transmission to national ministries; implementing regs set details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of special registers and public consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall maintain for all Member States special registers of patents, utility models, trademarks and service marks, industrial designs, trade names, geographical indications, plant variety certificates and layout designs, in which registrations shall be entered; any person may consult the registers and obtain extracts on the terms specified in the implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 18 — central register system with public access subject to implementing regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence of international agreements where diverging
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the provisions of this Agreement or its annexes diverge from those of the international agreements to which the Member States or the Organization are party, the international agreements shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 — international treaty obligations take precedence over Bangui Agreement when conflicts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding effect of final judicial decisions on validity of titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Final judicial decisions rendered in respect of the validity of titles in a Member State pursuant to the provisions of Annex I to Annex X shall be binding on all other Member States, save for decisions based on public policy and morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 20(1) — res judicata across Member States for title validity, with public policy/morality exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability of other final judicial decisions via exequatur
rubrics_metrics.description: Final judicial decisions rendered in a Member State in areas other than the validity of titles shall be enforceable in all other Member States pursuant to an exequatur decision rendered in accordance with the legislation of the State concerned, save for decisions based on public policy and morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 20(2) — other judgments require exequatur for cross-border enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and procedure for accession to the Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any African State that is not party to the Bangui Agreement but is party to the WIPO Convention, the Paris Convention, the Berne Convention and/or the Universal Copyright Convention and the Patent Cooperation Treaty may accede to this Agreement; application for accession submitted to the Administrative Council which rules by majority vote; accession takes effect two months after deposit of instrument unless later date specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 22(1)–(4) — accession prerequisites and administrative steps; equally divided votes constitute rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial obligations of Member States on accession and budget balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial financial contribution shall be required of any State that becomes a member; amount and terms determined by the Administrative Council; States recognized as ex-officio members shall be exempt; Member States shall make an exceptional contribution to balance the budget when required, distributed equally among Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 24(1)–(2) — initial and exceptional contributions, allocation rules set by Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council composition and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council shall be composed of representatives of the Member States on the basis of one representative per State; decisions taken as resolutions with each State having one vote; decisions generally by simple majority of members present or represented; in equally divided votes, the Chairperson has a casting vote; certain measures require unanimity as stated elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 26 and 30 — composition, voting procedure, and casting vote rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council functions and regulatory powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council is the highest authority; it shall determine overall policy, draft regulations necessary for implementation of the Agreement and Annexes, draft financial rules and regulations relating to fees, oversee application of regulations, approve program and yearly budget, audit and approve annual accounts, appoint senior executives and auditors, rule on membership applications, fix contributions, create ad hoc committees, and determine working languages of the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 27 — Council drafts/approves implementing regulations and oversees OAPI operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Commission of Appeal composition and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: The High Commission of Appeal shall be composed of three members selected by drawing of lots from a list of representatives designated by the Member States; it shall rule on appeals in cases of rejection of applications for titles of protection for industrial property, rejection of requests for maintenance or extension of terms, rejection of requests for restoration, and decisions on oppositions; sessions governed by rules adopted by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 31 — appellate body, limited to specified categories of administrative appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers and duties of the Director-General
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the authority of a Director-General, the Office is responsible for executive tasks and day-to-day management, implementing Administrative Council instructions; Director-General appointed for five-year renewable term, represents the Organization, drafts budget and reports, takes part in Council sessions without vote, recruits and dismisses staff (except most senior executives), decides whether to issue and maintain validity of titles and may impose penalties where empowered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 32–33 — Director-General holds operational authority including decision on issuance and validity of titles per delegated powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Arbitration and Mediation Center
rubrics_metrics.description: An Arbitration and Mediation Center is established within the Organization, attached to the Office of the Director-General, responsible for promoting extra-judicial resolution of IP disputes; organization and functioning fixed by regulations adopted by the Administrative Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 34 — internal ADR institution to facilitate non-judicial dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization resources and fee-setting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The resources of the Organization shall consist of proceeds from fees provided in regulations and Member State laws, proceeds from remuneration for services, other proceeds including property revenue, and donations/bequests approved by the Administrative Council; the Administrative Council shall lay down the fees and income necessary for running the Organization and fix their amounts and terms of payment; Member States may be required to make exceptional contributions to balance the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 35(1)–(3) — funding sources and Council's authority to set fees and require contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant variety owner maintenance and recording obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a plant variety certificate may be required to maintain or preserve the official sample himself; any change of ownership shall be recorded in writing, registered by the Organization and not binding on third parties unless recorded in the special register; Organization shall publish notice of change of ownership; licenses must be evidenced in writing and recorded in special plant varieties register and not binding on third parties until registered and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex X (PART VII) — transfer, licensing and maintenance obligations and registration/publication formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds for plant variety certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall deprive the owner of his plant variety certificate if established that he failed in obligation to preserve maintenance and the variety is no longer uniform or stable; also for failure to respond to verification requests or failure to propose a suitable denomination after notice; forfeiture may not be declared until owner put on formal notice to meet obligation within reasonable period; forfeiture takes effect on date of registration and is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex X (PART VII) — procedural safeguards before forfeiture (formal notice, reasonable period) and publication of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of procedural time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Organization deems such action justified by the circumstances, it may extend, on being so requested in writing, the time limit prescribed for performing an act or taking a step in accordance with this Annex or the Implementing Regulations by notifying its decision to the parties concerned; extension may be granted even if the time limit has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 44 (PART VIII) — OAPI has discretionary power to grant extensions on conditions it specifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil and criminal competent courts for plant variety matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil actions relating to plant varieties shall be brought before competent domestic courts and judged as summary proceedings; domestic court competent in criminal matters shall rule on arguments relating to infringement, invalidation or forfeiture of the plant variety certificate, or issues relating to ownership of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 45 (PART IX) — domestic courts handle civil and criminal matters; summary proceedings for civil actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation grounds for plant variety certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall invalidate the plant variety certificate if established that the variety was not new or distinct on the filing date or priority date, or where certificate was essentially based on applicant-submitted information the variety was not uniform or stable on the aforesaid date; an invalidated certificate is deemed invalid as of its date of issue; invalidation decision notified to Organization for registration and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 46 (PART IX) — substantive invalidation criteria (novelty/distinctness/uniformity/stability) and retroactive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement definitions and remedies for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any acts referred to in Article 31 carried out on the territory of a Member State by a person other than the owner of the plant variety certificate and without his consent shall constitute an infringement; acts prior to publication of issuance are not considered infringements except as of notification of certified true copy to alleged offender; courts may grant injunctions, damages and other remedies; licensees may institute actions and owners may participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 48–49 (PART IX) — infringement scope, exceptions, and remedies including emergency measures and injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure and border/customs measures for plant variety infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners of plant variety certificates may, under order from presiding judge, approach judicial officers to make description or seizure of allegedly infringing objects; customs may retain goods at written request of entitled persons accompanied by proof of right and must notify prosecutor, requester and owner; detention lifted automatically if requester fails within 10 working days to justify measures or show proceedings/guarantees; customs may act ex officio if presumptive evidence of infringement; customs liable for unjustified detention unless in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 50 and 60–61 (PART X) — judicial seizure and customs/detention procedures, 10-day rule and ex officio powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to institute substantive proceedings after seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: When measures to stop infringement are ordered prior to initiation of substantive proceedings, the applicant must initiate civil or criminal proceedings within 10 days from the next day following the date of adoption of the measure; failing this and at request of defendant the measures shall be cancelled without prejudice to damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 49(5) — strict 10-day deadline to begin substantive proceedings after interim measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quest for information powers of courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent domestic court may order, if petitioned, submission of all documents or information held by the defendant necessary to determine origin and distribution networks of infringing goods or processes, including names and addresses of producers, quantities produced/sold and prices, subject to financial compulsion if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 52 — broad disclosure powers to trace infringement chains and quantify commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of damages and penalty ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall determine damages taking into account negative economic consequences including loss of profits, profits made by infringer and moral prejudice; criminal penalties include fines between 5,000,000 and 15,000,000 CFA francs or imprisonment of one to six months or both, without prejudice to civil damages; other penalties permit confiscation and destruction where necessary and confiscated items may be auctioned for State benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 53–55 — classical damages standard plus specific criminal fine/imprisonment ranges and confiscation remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for criminal proceedings and extenuating circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal proceedings for application of penalties may be brought by the public prosecutor only on a complaint from the injured party; provisions on extenuating circumstances in domestic legislation shall apply to the offenses referred to in the Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 57–58 — criminal action requires complainant and domestic extenuating rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offences for usurpation and fraud in variety denominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who improperly avails himself of the status of owner of a plant variety certificate or of an application shall be liable to a fine of 5,000,000 to 15,000,000 CFA francs (doubled on repetition); any person who knowingly uses a designation in violation of Article 26(4) or fails to use a variety denomination in violation of Article 26(5) shall be liable to a fine of 2,000,000 to 5,000,000 CFA francs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 56 and 59 — specified monetary sanctions for usurpation and denomination fraud.
